findings.problem: _read opens files with newline="", so lone \r survives into the text passed to split_statements and conn.execute. splitlines treats \r as a line break, but SQLite line comments end only at \n. A comment followed by SQL in a CR-only file therefore becomes one chunk that SQLite treats as entirely comment. It runs as a no-op, the tracking row is inserted, and the migration is reported as applied although its SQL never ran, with no error. Default universal-newline reading would turn \r into \n and avoid this; the checksum does its own normalization, so newline="" isn't needed for it. Found by tracing the code and my knowledge of SQLite's comment handling; not executed, because my probe script was blocked by the permission check.
